title.narrative: Responsible Business Conduct in Latin America and Caribbean (OECD) - Bridge Grant

description.narrative:
Responsible Business Conduct in Latin America and the Caribbean (RBCLAC) implemented by OECD/ILO/UNOHCHR. It targets nine countries (AR, BR, CL, CO, CR, EC, ME, PA, PE). The Project aims to promote smart, sustainable and inclusive economic growth in the region by supporting responsible business conduct (RBC) practices in line with international instruments. The programme contains three main components:

-     Component 1. Supporting business capacity to conduct due diligence in priority sectors

-       Component 2. Strengthening the role of governments in promoting RBC

-       Component 3. Fostering workers¿ organisations and other stakeholder engagement for RBC

Under INTPA the project will increase the emphasis on supporting LAC stakeholders considering the EU¿s proposal for a directive on corporate sustainability due diligence and deforestation free products. Specific sectoral focus will be on mining and agriculture (including forestry).

comment.narrative: 2 processes related to RBC due diligence practices of businesses operating in LAC including in highrisk sectors their contributions to environmental protection decent working conditions and the respect of human rights have been influenced

The Project has directly contributed to increase the capacity of businesses in LAC to implement RBC due diligence. Notably the Project has supported the implementation of human rights due diligence in the sugarcane production sector in Costa Rica. Following a series of workshops CERALC has worked alongside the Sugar and Cane League LAICA composed of the 10 existing mills in the country in a sectoral process to identify the main adverse impacts on human rights labor rights and the environment. The resulting impact matrices will be used by LAICA and the sugar mills to characterise the impacts and to continue implementing the human rights due diligence processes. The Project is also accompanying LAICA in preparing a sectoral commitment to the UNGP and human rights due diligence.In addition within the Alliance for Human Rights and Businesses ADHE established in Brazil the Project contributed to the development and implementation of the BHR GAP Analysis Tool which marked a significant step forward in fostering accountability and awareness around business and human rights. This tool enables companies to conduct selfassessments on business and human rights and serves to collect data for research on human rights issues in the business sector in the country. The first results based on responses from 49 companies revealed i that companies are committed to human rights but fewer companies monitor the fulfillment of human rights commitments and ii that the measures adopted by companies to uphold their respect for human rights including training and mitigation measures as well as human rights impact assessments are more focused on risks and impacts related to employees and less on risks and impacts related to their supply chains and operational surroundings.

The Project has directly contributed to improved coherence of government policies that promote RBC and to maintain engagement on RBC. One example is the achievements made in Peru where the Project has accompanied the Ministry of Justice in the implementation of the commitments included in the National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights 20212025 including the consolidation of regional public policy on RBC in provincial cities such as Piura and Ica. The effects of the NAP were also evaluated in coordination with civil society organisations and the Ministry of Justice. Likewise the Project has also been key for advancing in the implementation of the EU Deforestation Regulation. In this regard the Project started collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and the Ministry of Labour to implement reporting mechanisms traceability and due diligence procedures. Another example is the development of Colombias National Policy on Business and Human Rights which is expected to be adopted in 2025 through a presidential decree the highest regulatory level for such a policy in the country. During the bridge grant phase the Project established a formal Policymakers Roundtable on RBC providing a structured platform for dialogue and consultation among key governmental entities involved in shaping the policy. This roundtable led by the Office of the Presidential Advisor for Human Rights with technical support from the NCP for RBC in the Ministry of Trade has facilitated strategic coordination and capacitybuilding. The policy is set to align Colombias business practices with international RBC standards ensuring a comprehensive approach to addressing preventing and mitigating risks related to human rights within business operations and supply chains.

During the Bridge phase the Project successfully engaged unions and other stakeholders in dialogue to advance the uptake of RBC. In particular under the leadership of the Confederation of Workers of the Americas trade unions from Costa Rica Ecuador Argentina Peru Chile Panama and Mexico conducted national workshops on RBC and developed an action plan with the aim to foster knowledge regarding the RBC international instruments and to strengthen the capacities of workers organisations. The ultimate goal is to equipe workers organisations with the necessary knowledge to participate in the discussion of the national policies led by the governments ensuring that their visions and proposals are taken into account.Another practical example is the Community of Practice developed by the Project. This Community has remained active since 2021 delivering significant results through its 33 sessions since its inception. These sessions have provided a platform for capacity building and knowledge exchange on critical topics related to the Business and Human Rights agenda fostering collaboration among state officials experts from national governments international organisations civil society and the European Union. In the first half of 2024 the sessions addressed topics such as Challenges in the Effective Implementation of the Escaz Agreement Towards the Development of Public Policies in the Region. The most recent session held in June 2024 focused on European Regulations on Due Diligence and Their Implementation in Latin America bringing in expertise from the European Commission.

During the period JanuaryNovember 2024 the Project has successfully influenced approaches and practices on RBC in the region including1.Awareness and commitment about RBC increased the Project played a key role in advancing RBC by providing technical contributions at the multistakeholder forum titled Business Integrity and Due Diligence in Supply Chains organised by GIZ in Mexico and Alliance for Integrity. The forum resulted in the development of a roadmap outlining concrete initiatives to promote respect for human rights and due diligence in global supply chains. Key outcomes include the creation of the Responsible Business Helpdesk the establishment of the Human Rights Complaint Mechanism MRDH for the automotive sector and the launch of Phase II of the RBC LAC project. The forum reflects the collective commitment of different actors to building a responsible and sustainable future for global supply chains. press note attached2.National policies supporting RBC in Brazil strengthened the Project provided technical support to the Coordination of Businesses and Human Rights within the Ministry of Human Rights and Citizenship of Brazil and participated in and contributed to the Hearing of Experts for the design of the Business and Human Rights Policy. In addition the Project also participated in an event organised by civil society and social movements aimed at submitting recommendations to the policy text where the Project was responsible for defining the methodology and systematising the results. The Project also participated in and provided technical contribution to the public hearing held by the Federal Prosecutors Office to discuss Bill PL 5722022 which was presented to establish a legal framework on businesses and human rights in the country.
